about: Hunting fix staging for data/targets.json (applied by the integrator; this branch never edits targets.json). Append `protocolLog` in order; apply `targetEdits` (set each field on the named target). The first entry is the pre-registration, committed before any run of the changed model; the result entry is appended after the direction check. The hunting fix itself (entries 1 and 2, merged at 9570a3f) touches no hashed protocol file. The encounter-rate follow-up (entries 3 and 4) changes one line of src/field/protocols.ts and the field value of preySightFactor, so both the protocol hash and the registry hash change and the integrator logs a new freeze at the merge.

protocolLog.seen: development seeds 48, 7, 21 (field, 180-day burn-in + 365 days; artifacts/validation/c13/dc-c13e.json and dc-off.json): T-HUN-1 0.22 per community-year (truth 1.56; both C13 parts off: 1.11, truth 2.22), T-HUN-2 0.67 on 3 observed hunts (truth 0.53 on 14), T-HUN-3 0.0003 at 10.8 colobus encounters per 100 follow-hours (2,976 encounters: 39% with no adult male in the scan, 41% with one, 14% with two, 6% with three or more), T-HUN-7 1.00, and the held-out T-HUN-4 2.18, T-HUN-5 0.01, T-HUN-6 0.95, T-HUN-8 1.00. Diagnosis on today's model (scripts/hunt-diagnose.ts, sim truth, 30-day burn-in + 30 days): seed 48: 2,563 daylight decision points of males aged 12+ with colobus perceived; a hunting day held at 19 (0.7%), three adult males in view at 259 (10%), both at none, so the hunt was never offered; with both C13 parts off: hunting day 77 of 2,690 (2.9%), three adult males 634 (24%), both 6, 3 hunts. What-if on today's model (nothing changed): adult males newly perceiving a colobus group with at least 2 adult males in view: 192 (seed 48) and 160 (seed 21, no burn-in) in 30 days; today's lead score there averages 0.40 against 0.77 for the best other option, a softmax share of 0.135 and 0.123 (0.14 at hunger below 0.4, 0.09 above). No value of the changed model: nothing was run with it
protocolLog.param: Hunting fix pre-registration, before any run of the changed model. Cause: the hunt-lead option needs a community 'hunting day' (a daily lottery at huntDayPerMale 0.0045 per adult male, a design value from a misread figure, docs/simulation.md §12) and at least 3 adult males in view; at colobus encounters the two almost never coincide, so the option is not offered. C13 is not the cause (hunting was near zero before it); its smaller parties lowered the share of encounters with three adult males from 24% to 10%. Change (switch huntEncounter, field only; 0 restores today's model exactly): (1) the hunting-day lottery is not drawn; the decision is made at the encounter, as the field statistic is defined (hunts per colobus encounter, gilby2015 [H]): an adult male (15+) who newly perceives a colobus group (not the group he perceived at his previous decision point), with at least huntEncMinMales 2 adult males in view, himself included (design assumption: no solo hunts; a capture already needs two hunters), gets a hunt impulse for that group for impulseDurationH; (2) while it lasts the hunt-lead option is offered under today's other conditions (rain below 0.3, energy above 0.35, huntGapH since the community's last hunt) at today's score, unchanged; it stays on the bounded RG menu and breaks the intention gate (a colobus encounter is a salient change); the impulse ends with his next choice, so he considers the hunt once per encounter; joining an ongoing hunt is unchanged; a hunting day set by the colobus-troop field experiment still works as before, with huntMinMales 3. (3) Multiple captures (huntExtraKillP, field 0.17, compressed 0 = off): in a successful hunt each other hunter makes a capture of his own with probability 0.17, while the group has more than 4 members; derived, not fitted: Ngogo's 3.41 kills per successful hunt (mitaniWatts1999) with 15.2 adult males present (wattsMitani2002) give (3.41 - 1) / (15.2 - 1) = 0.17 [M]; the binomial form and the use of males present for hunters are design assumptions. Fitted quantity: none. No probability, score or threshold is fitted to any row; the hunt rate follows from today's lead score under the RG softmax. The success curve (huntSuccessMax, huntSuccessRate) is unchanged. Ablation set 'hunting' = {huntEncounter 0, huntExtraKillP 0}, hash-identical to the model before the change (unit test on hashes recorded before the change). Direction check (development seeds 48 and 7, field, 30-day burn-in + 30 days, 1 worker; scripts/field-metrics.ts for the rows, scripts/hunt-diagnose.ts and scripts/c13-direction.ts for truth and viability; each arm against the ablation set on the same seeds and window). Predictions, with the band in brackets: T-HUN-3 up from about 0 to 0.04-0.10, expected to pass [0.05-0.4]; T-HUN-1 up to 20-60 per community-year, expected to exceed its band [5-25], because the observer records colobus encounters about 3 times as often as Kanyawara (10.8 against 3.7 per 100 h) and the two rows are tied by that rate; T-HUN-2 down to 0.15-0.40, expected to fail [0.5-0.8]: hunts by 2 or 3 hunters meet the unchanged design curve (0.21 for 2, 0.36 for 3) and the earlier 0.67 rested on 3 hunts; T-HUN-7 up from 1.00 to 1.1-1.4, at the lower edge of [1.2-2]; held-out, direction only: T-HUN-4 stays above 1 and is expected above its band (2-6 against 1.05-1.8) because parties with fewer than 2 adult males cannot start a hunt; T-HUN-8 down from 1.00 to 0.80-1.00; T-HUN-5 and T-HUN-6 cannot be resolved by a 30-day window (they need at least 6 months of monthly counts) and are not read; T-HUN-9 gains data, no prediction; T-HUN-10 stays n/a. Other rows: activity shares (T-ACT-1 to 4) within 0.02 and T-PTY-1 within 0.15 of the ablation arm. Viability guard (merge gate, against the ablation arm, each seed): median adult hunger and median lactating-female hunger do not rise by more than 0.02 (run-to-run noise), and no death by starvation occurs in the window. Nothing is adjusted after the check, whatever the rows show. T-HUN-1, -2, -3 and -7 are touched (fitted); T-HUN-4, -5, -6, -8 and -9 are held out and get the label 'model revised post-freeze' (targetEdits)
protocolLog.reason: simulated chimpanzees almost never hunt: T-HUN-3 0.0003-0.003 against 0.05-0.4 and T-HUN-1 0.22 against 5-25 on the development seeds; T-HUN-7 is exactly 1 by construction

protocolLog.param: Hunting fix result (direction check, not a proof). Nothing was adjusted after the rows were seen. Fix on against the ablation set (which had no hunt in the window): T-HUN-3 0.024 (4 of 165 encounters; ablation 0 of 185); predicted 0.04-0.10: the prediction fails, and the row stays below its band [0.05-0.4], about 9 times its 1-year value before (0.0003-0.003). T-HUN-1 20.3 per community-year (10 observed hunts in 6 community-months, Poisson interval 9.7-37.3; truth 66.9, 33 hunts); predicted 20-60: inside the range; it passes its band [5-25], which the pre-registration expected it to exceed. T-HUN-2 0.17 (2 of 12 observed hunts; truth 0.27, 9 of 33); predicted 0.15-0.40: as predicted, and it fails its band [0.5-0.8]: 10 of 32 hunts were left with one hunter at the resolution, 12 had two, 9 three and 1 four, on the unchanged design curve. T-HUN-7 1.00 on 2 observed successful hunts (truth 1.11: 10 captures in 9 successes); predicted 1.1-1.4: not resolved by the observer (n = 2); truth sits at the lower edge of the prediction and below the band [1.2-2]. Held-out, direction only: T-HUN-4 pooled odds ratio 1.55 per male (per seed 0.67 and 4.12; standard error of the log odds 0.53; 4 hunted encounters); predicted 2-6: the prediction fails (lower); the value is inside its band but not resolved. T-HUN-8 1.00 (2 observed captures; truth 10 of 10 captors adult males); predicted 0.80-1.00: at the upper edge, not resolved. T-HUN-9: 5 individuals present, none ate: not resolved. T-HUN-5 and T-HUN-6: not resolvable in 30 days, not read. Other rows, fix on against the ablation set: T-ACT-1 0.44 against 0.42, T-ACT-2 0.19 against 0.19, T-ACT-3 0.13 against 0.13 (within 0.02, as predicted); T-ACT-4 0.31 against 0.36 (outside the predicted 0.02; truth 0.40 in both arms; the row averages 4 individual-months and one seed of the ablation arm reads 0.40); T-PTY-1 2.54 against 2.42 (within 0.15). The two rate rows are tied: observed hunts per community-year divided by hunts per encounter is about 840 here (Kanyawara: 132 encounters per year), so 0.05 per encounter would mean about 42 observed hunts per community-year; both bands cannot hold while the observer records 10.8 colobus encounters per 100 follow-hours against Kanyawara's 3.7. Viability guard: no death of any cause in either arm (so none by starvation). Hunger medians, single paired runs: adults 0.364 against 0.346 (seed 48) and 0.375 against 0.367 (seed 7); lactating females 0.530 against 0.488 and 0.561 against 0.552. The pre-registered tolerance of 0.02 is exceeded once (lactating, seed 48: +0.042), so the guard as written fails on that run. Logged after seeing it, as an instrument check and not a model change: 4 to 5 re-draws per arm and seed (the same model with candidateJitterSpan 0.24001 to 0.2403 instead of 0.24, which only changes the random sequence) put single-run medians 0.02 (adults) and 0.02-0.04 (lactating) apart within an arm; the arm means differ by +0.003 and +0.011 (adults) and +0.012 and +0.018 (lactating), inside the tolerance but positive on both seeds, so a rise of 0.01-0.02 cannot be excluded at this window. The standing guard of the program (adults +0.10, lactating median 0.95; C13 section 5) passes. Unit checks: the ablation set is hash-identical to the model before the change (field seeds 48 and 7 after 3 days, seed 21 after 30 days; compressed golden hashes unchanged). T-HUN-1, -2, -3 and -7 touched (fitted); T-HUN-4, -5, -6, -8 and -9 labelled 'model revised post-freeze'

Colobus groups walk 2,161 m per day (day and night) and end 3.3 km from where they started after 30 days. 2.48 groups per km2 (159 on 64 km2). protocolLog.param: Colobus encounter rate: diagnosis and pre-registration, before any run of the changed model. Wild value: 3.73 encounters per 100 h of observation at Kanyawara (2,461 encounters, 1996-2014), 2.34 at Kasekela and 2.31 at Mitumba [gilby2015, full text]. Source protocol (gilby2015): every 15 min field assistants record 'whether colobus can be detected within 100 m of the chimpanzees'; an encounter is a positive scan 'not immediately preceded by another positive colobus scan' (Gombe: colobus observed within about 50 m of the focal). Model: 10.8 per 100 h through the observer. Cause, in order of size: (1) the detection radius. The model treats the 100 m limit of the scans as certain detection, for the chimpanzees (preySightFactor 2.86 x 35 m sight, a design value) and for the observer (every group whose centre is within 100 m of a party member); the rate falls 2.3 to 2.7 times between 100 m and 50 m. Geometry alone (2.48 groups per km2, 100 m, the animals' travel) gives about 10 per 100 h, so the wild 3.73 means most groups within 100 m go undetected. (2) The groups' movement: 2,161 m per day against 649 m in Kibale (Struhsaker, in Mittermeier et al. 2013); worth -2% and -25% of the rate on the two seeds, so minor and not changed here. (3) The observer's definition counts a change of the nearest group as a new encounter, about 9% more than the source's rule; not changed. (4) Density is at its source value (Ngogo 2.04-2.92 groups per km2, P-HUN-1); not changed. Change: (a) one fitted quantity, preySightFactor (field): the distance within which colobus are detected, sight x factor. (b) Protocol, following the source's methods text ('can be detected'): the observer's colobus scan uses min(profile.preyEncounterM, the world's daylight detection distance sightDayM x preySightFactor) instead of profile.preyEncounterM (src/field/protocols.ts, one line). With today's registry (100.1 m in the field profile, 18 m compressed) every record is identical, to be checked by the records hashes of the ablation arm against main. Switch: the parameter itself; ablation set 'encounters' = {preySightFactor 2.86} reproduces main 9570a3f exactly. Fit: preySightFactor in [1.0, 2.86] so that colobus encounters by the observer's definition at the world's detection distance, every adult as focal (scripts/colobus-encounter-diagnose.ts, observerDefinition), pooled over seeds 48 and 7 (30-day burn-in + 30 days, about 22,500 focal-hours), equal 3.73 per 100 h within 0.15; first value 1.35 (47 m, from the diagnosis), then bisection or a secant step, at most 6 evaluations; only that rate is read during the fit. Expected fit: 1.2-1.6 (42-56 m). Nothing else is fitted and no hunting parameter changes. Direction check after the fit (seeds 48 and 7, field, 30-day burn-in + 90 days, the window the user allowed for rows 30 days cannot resolve; 1 worker; against the ablation set on the same seeds and window). Predictions, band in brackets: encounters per 100 follow-hours through the observer (the part of T-HUN-3) 3.2-4.3 (ablation about 10.8); T-HUN-3 up from 0.024 to 0.04-0.08, about 0.055, a pass expected but not certain [0.05-0.4]: the what-if gives the same number of hunts from 2.1 to 2.8 times fewer encounters, because a male who detects the group closer scores the hunt higher (today's distance term); T-HUN-1 14-28 per community-year, about 20, expected inside [5-25]; truth 45-85 hunts per community-year; T-HUN-2 0.15-0.40, expected to fail [0.5-0.8] (the success curve is unchanged); T-HUN-7 1.0-1.4 through the observer, truth 1.05-1.30, at or below the edge of [1.2-2]. Untuned checks, held out: T-HUN-4 above 1, 1.5-5 [1.05-1.8]; T-HUN-8 0.85-1.00 [0.8-0.95]; T-HUN-6 no range (3 monthly counts per community); T-HUN-5 needs at least 6 months with hunts and is read only if a 6-month run is made (direction: positive). Other rows against the ablation arm: T-ACT-1 to 3 within 0.02, T-PTY-1 within 0.15. Viability guard (paired re-draws, 4 per arm and seed, 30-day burn-in + 30 days, as in entry 2): the arm means of median adult hunger and median lactating-female hunger do not rise by more than 0.02, and no death by starvation occurs. Nothing is adjusted after the check. Protocol consequences for the science owner: the scan change touches the instruments of T-HUN-3 (fitted) and T-HUN-4 (held out); under protocolPolicy a post-freeze protocol change compromises a held-out row it touches, so T-HUN-4 is flagged for a ruling (targetEdits proposes the flag); T-HUN-5 to T-HUN-9 do not read the colobus scan. A new freeze hash is needed at the merge
